source_checks.finding: Section 'Set alarm time' confirms: 'On the digital clock: Enter the hour and minutes you want.'; 'With the 12-hour format: Tap AM or PM.'; 'Tap OK.'; 'To add an alarm, tap Add'; 'Tap Alarm.' Step 1 on the page reads 'Open your device's Clock app' (passage says 'Open the Clock app'; same action, wording differs only). Verified excerpt on the page: 'Important: If you set 2 alarms too close together, the first one may be canceled. To make sure both alarms work, leave a 5-minute window between each alarm.' The page says the steps apply to 'your Android device, Pixel phone, or Pixel Tablet' and names no Android version or model, which matches the ref's applicability.

required_actions.action: Open the Clock app and tap Alarm
Tap Add to create a new alarm
Enter the hour and minutes on the digital clock, since the user cannot drag the hands
With the 12-hour format, tap AM or PM
Tap OK to save the alarm
Leave a 5-minute window between alarms if more than one is set (conditional)

source_checks.finding: Page confirms 'Open the Clock app, then tap the Alarms tab.', 'Tap the Add button.', 'Tap to name your alarm.' (Label), 'Turn on to see a Snooze option when the alarm sounds and set a Snooze Duration.' (Snooze), and the final save step, which the page words as 'Save the alarm with the Done button' (the passage's 'Tap the Done button.' is the same action). The page mentions iOS 27 only in an alarm-volume section, not in these steps, and names no minimum iOS version or iPhone model for these steps, which matches the ref's applicability. The earlier assistant turn (Clock app, Alarms tab, Add, set a time, Done) matches this page.

Android distractor. The page is for Android devices and Pixel phones and Tablets (confirmed, no Android version named), so it does not apply to this iPhone user and is correctly unused. The verified excerpt 'To make sure both alarms work, leave a 5-minute window between each alarm.' is on the page.

required_actions.action: Tap Label and name the alarm Pills
Turn on Snooze and set a Snooze Duration
Tap Done to save the alarm
Already completed by user (not needed): open Alarms tab, tap Add, set 7:00

source_checks.finding: The en-us address returned PROVENANCE_REQUIRED and was not retried; the search returned https://support.apple.com/en-ng/105001 for the same article, and the checks were made there. The page confirms 'Press and hold the Flashlight button' and 'Drag the slider up or down to adjust brightness.' It also confirms the Control Center opening steps used in the earlier assistant turn: 'Swipe down from the upper-right corner to open Control Center on your iPhone' and, for an iPhone with a Home button, swipe up from the bottom. The page names iOS 26 only in an image caption and gives no minimum iOS version for these steps, which matches the ref's applicability.

Distractor. The page is for Galaxy phones (it names Galaxy S21, Galaxy S25 Ultra and XCover6 Pro in captions and text) and names no Android version. It confirms 'The brightness slider will be grayed out if you don't turn on the flashlight first.' This does not apply to this iPhone user and is correctly unused.

required_actions.action: Press and hold the Flashlight button in Control Center
Drag the slider up or down to change brightness
Already completed by user (not needed): turned the flashlight on from Control Center
Open Control Center first if it has closed (page lead-in for the brightness steps; not in the passage)

source_checks.finding: Section 'Pair and connect your hearing device: iPhone or iPad' confirms 'Make sure that iOS or iPadOS is up to date.', open Settings, Accessibility, then Hearing Devices, 'Pair MFi Hearing Device, then follow the onscreen instructions.', selecting the available hearing device and tapping Pair, the fallback to tap the name of the hearing device when it appears in Hearing Devices settings, and tapping Pair when Bluetooth pairing requests appear. The page names no iOS version number, which matches the ref. The lead-in also says the pairing follows after checking compatibility and putting the device in pairing mode; the passage does not include that point, so it is not a required action under the passage-only rule.

Distractor. The page is about Bluetooth devices near an Android device; it confirms 'Tap Pair new device.' in the Settings section and the warning that 'Some of these steps work only on Android 15 and up' without naming which steps. It does not apply to this iPhone user and is correctly unused.

required_actions.action: Make sure iOS or iPadOS is up to date
Open Settings, then tap Accessibility, then tap Hearing Devices
Tap Pair MFi Hearing Device and follow the onscreen instructions
Select your hearing device and tap Pair
Tap Pair when Bluetooth pairing requests appear
If Pair MFi Hearing Device is missing, tap the device name in Hearing Devices settings (conditional)
Put the hearing aids in pairing mode (page lead-in only; not in the passage, so not a required action under the passage-only rule)
